verified_fixes: Guard: I ran guard.sh myself on 05d93b3 and it printed GUARD: ALL GREEN (fmt, clippy -D warnings, all tests, doctests, MSRV 1.75, wasm, rustdoc -D warnings).

Q1 (one head size): every flowchart end glyph is 11 px, markerUnits=userSpaceOnUse, glyph `M 0 0 L 10 5 L 0 10 z`. This covers the thick `==>` edge (stroke 3.5 shares #arrow), arrow-start, cross-end/start and circle-end/start. linkStyle colours reach the markers (arrow-t8__e33, cross-start__00f, cross-end__00f in my x1_styles input). The advance painter uses the shared scene::arrow_marker_def: advance_swimlane now has refX 5 and 11 px, where before it had refX 8.5 and 7 units.

M1 (cut under the head): the painted stroke stops ARROW_TRIM = 5.5 px short of the tip; a width over 5.5 is cut by its own width, at most 11. refX puts the tip exactly on the border: in demo A→B the path ends at y=108.5 and the tip is at 114.0, the border. At 16x zoom the thick D→F head and the 8 px red linkStyle head show no butt-end pixels outside the triangle and no overshoot. SceneEdge.bezier is unchanged for single cubics; long edges get a straight stub in their waypoints (edgepass::glyph_stubs, which runs in finish_fixed for static and routed modes alike).
Q10 stroke tokens: edges 2 px, thick 3.5 px, node outlines 1.8 px including the hard-coded ones, SVG padding 16.
Non-flowchart renderers are byte-identical before and after the package: class, er, sequence, pie, journey, timeline, gitgraph, sankey, mindmap, architecture, in both cmp/corpus and examples.

Interactive contract: a scratch crate (verify/b1-arrows/ix3) checked 14 corpus flowcharts, the state examples and 6 new stress inputs. It built scene() and route(), moved 4 nodes x 4 offsets, and called route() and route_partial(). Results: SceneEdge index-parallel with Graph::edges everywhere; output deterministic (scene, route, route_partial and to_svg each byte-equal when run twice); to_mermaid round-trip unchanged.

Pick == render: every sampled point on every painted stroke picks an edge at tol 0. In static and routed scenes, edge_at(tol 4) agreed with the nearest painted stroke (head region modelled) on 100% of random points. In drag scenes it agreed on 99.99%; the only mismatches are degenerate nearly-touching nodes (see problems).

Round-3 picking speed (#2): whole-canvas hits_in_rect is faster than before the package (bench-75 0.021 -> 0.006 ms, dense-td 0.012 -> 0.004 ms). Hover is 10.7-23 µs on the dense files, which were 13-28 µs before. Small files went from about 0.4-1.3 µs to 1-6 µs, which still does not matter.

Round-3 to_svg speed (#1): I measured full render_svg with `bench files`, median ms before -> now. bench-75 45.8 -> 36.6, dense-td 26.5 -> 32.0, dense-lr 24.0 -> 26.5, fanout-frames 2.7 -> 3.0, syn200 83 -> 99, syn400 93 -> 131, syn1000 195 -> 287. All are within the 2x static budget; the 3-9x slowdown from the earlier round is gone.

Round-3 #4 (crowded heads): x6_fan's four thick heads on Sink are drawn as arrow-w8_5 with gaps between them. Before the package they merged into one blob (the 2x heads). x2_crowd's 8 heads on one side are all square with gaps of 3 px or more.
Round-3 #5 and #6: an_advance_route_with_a_short_last_leg_keeps_its_head_on_that_leg is present and passing. Metrics is #[non_exhaustive], with a Breaking note in the CHANGELOG.

Spec success criteria: a thick head is the same size as a normal head. Heads within 10 deg of the side normal, back-edge bows excluded: 96.7% static and 95.1% routed (the perf corpus has 257 edges, 12 of them bows). The B0 ratchet was lowered: end_tilt 24 -> 14 static, end_kink added at 60|77. diagrams_without_link_style_render_exactly_as_before was updated with the reason given; edge_markers_draw_at_the_right_ends is unchanged and passes.

Tests are not weakened: the only removed assertions were replaced by stricter ones for the new marker ids. There are no #[ignore]. Gates loosened, each with a reason in a comment: BORDER_LEN_MAX static 1070 -> 1082, idiom_spline static 19 -> 25 (edges reclassified), lat_backtrack routed 674 -> 676, band_len routed 46446 -> 46604. The rest were lowered. No new dependency; no debug leftovers (the thread_local SQUARED counter is #[cfg(test)]). CHANGELOG [Unreleased] and README are updated.

Drag budget per PLAN invariant 1, three perf.sh runs. bench-75 route_ms was 18.05 on the first run (limit 15.76) and 13.70 / 12.02 on the re-runs. dense-td drag_ms was 14.65 / 14.64 / 18.07 (limit 17.8). fanout-frames drag_ms was 3.36 / 2.31 / 2.37 (limit 3.44). Medians are within budget and defects are unchanged on every file (static 69, routed 98). route_partial max is 5.3-6.8 ms on bench-75, against 5.5-6.4 ms before the package (same noise).
problems:
BLOCKING: edges are clipped off the canvas. Q10 was done as SVG padding only: SVG_MARGIN is 16 (src/scene.rs:45, used at to_svg ~4775) while the scene keeps its 28 px MARGIN gutter. The router may route in that gutter: src/router.rs:125 `ROUTE_OUTER = MARGIN / 2`, commented 'so a detour round the outermost node stays on the canvas'. grow_scene (src/scene.rs:5181) adds only e.bezier and curve_geometry for an edge, never its waypoint spline or route. Routes up to about 28 px beyond the drawing used to fit inside the 28 px padding; with 16 they now fall off the canvas.

Corpus evidence: advanced.mmd in route() mode (quality --svg advanced.routed.svg). The vertical leg of Scan → Dev 'fail' sits at x=723.0 in a 721-wide viewBox, so the whole 2 px stroke is outside; before the package it was at 735.0 in 745. The rendered PNG shows the dashed edge leaving the canvas on the right and coming back.

Extra inputs: in ex3/x3_long.mmd (static) the start → a1 leg is at x=-11.8 in a 292-wide viewBox, only two stubs are visible, and the vertical run is gone; before it was at 0.2. In 60 random flowcharts (verify/b1-arrows/rnd) the package newly clips r56 (n7 → n11 at x=950.7, viewBox width 938; before 962.7 in 962) and r22 (2.8 px). It makes r01 and r31 12 px worse (17.9 -> 29.9 and 20.5 -> 32.5 px past the canvas).

Suggested fix: grow the SVG canvas over the drawn curve, e.g. edge_polyline or the painted segments plus half the stroke, in grow_scene or at least in to_svg. Alternatively keep the painted padding at least as wide as the gutter the router can use. Add a quality gate for strokes outside the viewBox.

NON-BLOCKING: M1's 'last head length straight' still fails for about a third of glyph ends. end_kink on the perf corpus is 85/257 static and 101/257 routed; the gate fixtures give 60|77. A square head on a turning S-cubic shows an elbow or hook at the head base. Example: advanced Gate → Job Queue (thick) paints `... 186.7 184.8 C 185.4 186.5, 182.1 187.1, 182.1 189.2 L 182.1 192.0`, a 5 px hook that is visible at 2.5x zoom. In fanout-frames n0 → g1 the stroke arrives nearly vertical into a head pointing right (an L-shape). The implementer documents this as needing a different edge shape.

NON-BLOCKING: routed end_tilt barely moved (25 -> 24 on the perf corpus). Sixteen bench-75 routed ends still face 73-128 deg off the side normal (job1->ext and dash->ext 128.4 deg, svc4->metrics 116.6 deg), unchanged from before the package; they are ports-stage ends turned round a corner. The 95% criterion holds only barely in routed mode (95.1%).

NON-BLOCKING: a very wide linkStyle stroke ends badly. ex3/x1_styles.mmd, `linkStyle 2 stroke-width:14px`, paints `... C 139.6 220.4, 142.0 221.6, 144.4 222.6 L 145.9 222.6` with marker arrow-t11__3a3 (refX 0). The 14 px butt end is wider than the 11 px head and has a notched corner where the slanted curve meets the 1.5 px level run (verify/b1-arrows/z3/x1_green.png).

NON-BLOCKING (drag-only, degenerate): when a curve is shorter than trim + 1 px (nodes about 4-6 px apart mid-drag), the stroke is drawn whole and the refX 5 head reaches 5.5 px past the curve's end into the target node. Picking does not cover that ink. Example: fanout drag scene, e2 A->B3, bezier (460.85,126) -> (464.95,126.23); the painted head tip lands at about (470.4,126.4).
NON-BLOCKING: to_svg is slower on large synthetic graphs (render_svg syn400 93 -> 131 ms, syn1000 195 -> 287 ms), because the painter squares each turning end. This is within the 2x static budget.
unfixed_items: Q10 MARGIN 16 in scene coordinates (layout.rs): done only as the SVG padding (SVG_MARGIN) while the scene and router keep the 28 px gutter. The reason for the skip (float-exact router tie-breaks would move routes) is plausible. As built, though, the skip is NOT legitimate yet: it clips routed edges (see the blocking problem). Either the canvas must cover the drawn routes, or the router's outer room must fit within SVG_MARGIN.

M1: router end stub >= 2*ARROW_MARKER_PX + corner radius (router.rs, ROUTE_CLEAR + STUB_EXTRA): skipped. Lengthening the stub in the search moved dense-fixture routes (+12-40% overlap/tight); the attempt is kept as b1/router_longstub.patch. Given the 'no other layout change' constraint and the later routing packages, the skip is legitimate.

M1: last head length straight for strongly turning single cubics, done in the scene: skipped. The painter squares an end only within about 1 px of the scene curve, and falls back to entering along the tangent line; end_kink 60|77 remain. The case that a cubic cannot do it (handles capped at half the border gap) is credible; it belongs to the orthogonal or edge-shape work (report §2.1). Legitimate, but the visible elbows remain.
Report §2.4 ports-stage spreading of ends on over-full sides: out of B1's scope. The painter-side narrowing (arrow-w markers) is an acceptable interim.
notes:
Verdict is fail on one blocking item: the clipping regression that comes from making the SVG padding 16 px while the router still routes in the 28 px scene gutter. Everything else in the package checks out.

**Checks**
- Guard is green.
- Perf medians are within the drag budget; one noisy run each of bench-75 route_ms and dense-td drag_ms was over the limit, and the re-runs were within it.
- Quality defects are unchanged on every corpus file.
- B0 metrics against the pre-package worktree:
  - Improved: end_tilt 33->20 static, 25->24 routed; xgap_max 11->9; tight_len.
  - Small rises:
    - bench-75 routed: border_len 223->274, overlap_len 2448->2478, hug_runs 10->11.
    - dense-lr routed: overlap_len 698->714.
  - These come from measuring the straight painted stubs. Routed border_len in total fell (2030->2015). The one static gate raised (BORDER_LEN_MAX) is justified in its comment.

**Visual review**
- I looked at all 14 flowchart corpus three-way PNGs plus state, the bench-75 and fanout-frames tip grids (pre against now at 4x), the advance examples, and 6 stress inputs: styles/linkStyle widths, an over-full side, frames with long edges, state, shapes, and a thick fan.
- Heads are clearly better than before: the thick 2x heads and merged blobs are gone, tips sit on borders and heads into frames are square.
- The remaining ugliness is elbows at the head base on S-curves, back-edge bows (B3) and port crowding.

**Advance swimlane**
- The green dotted Auth -> API Gateway head is now hidden under the navy loop edge's equal-size head; both end at (100.6,187.5).
- This is an existing shared-port overlap, not caused by B1. Before, the green head was simply bigger.

- It is documented under Breaking within the same unreleased cycle, so it is acceptable.
